summary.en: KERN splits interactive elements into controls, which trigger an action immediately, and inputs, which collect data and usually need separate confirmation. The split shows up in the styling: controls use the action colour tokens, inputs the form-input tokens, so users can tell at a glance whether a screen asks them to act or to enter something.
Interactive elements fall into two groups, controls and inputs. The distinction is functional and is mirrored in the visual design with dedicated tokens, which keeps user guidance clear.

Controls trigger an action straight away, such as buttons and links that confirm, open, move or filter. They use --kern-color-action-* tokens for background and text; how much of the action colour is applied signals priority, from filled primary to outlined secondary to text-only tertiary.

Inputs collect data from users, including text fields, checkboxes and radios. They usually are not tied to an action and need separate confirmation such as a "Continue" button. They use the --kern-color-form-input-* tokens, with text following the general layout text tokens.

sections.heading: Beispiel für die Anwendung der verschiedenen Token

summary.en: Input File shows both kinds at once: its field and label are inputs and use the form-input tokens, while the button that opens the file browser is a control using the action tokens, since it acts immediately. KERN asks authors to keep this token logic so users can tell an action from data entry.
Controls trigger actions and use the action tokens; inputs collect data, need confirmation, and use the form-input tokens.
